transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for being here. So as we all know, the family wants to preserve several of our older relatives' stories in recordings that future family members can listen to. I've got the only working camcorder, so I'm coordinating the recording evening and deciding how the files will be handled afterward. The recordings will include both video and spoken audio, and we've got our shared digital drive for family materials where we can store everything. Before I confirm any plan, I'd like to do what I usually do -- get Nina's and Omar's preferences and practical advice first. So, Nina, do you have any thoughts on how we should approach the recording evening -- timing, format, anything like that?

transcript.text: Before we finalize any plan, I want to share something important. I haven't had a chance to tell you both this until now, but I think we need to make sure that's part of our plan.

transcript.text: Thanks, Nina -- that's a really important point about keeping the recordings in the family archive only, and I think we should definitely build that into the plan. I also want to share some advice I got that I haven't mentioned yet. My friend Priya, who's an audiovisual archivist, told me that for preserving oral histories like this, the audio should be captured as uncompressed WAV files at exactly 48 kHz and 24-bit depth, and we should make two verified backup copies. That way we're not just saving the video from the camcorder but also preserving the best possible audio quality for future family members. I think we should factor those specs into how we handle the files afterward on the shared drive.

I want to make sure whatever we decide is actually achievable before I confirm the plan.

transcript.text: Thanks, Maya. I'm glad my grandmother's preference is an easy yes -- that gives me confidence we're on the same page. On timing and format, I'd suggest we keep each interview session to about 30 to 45 minutes so the older relatives don't get too tired, and maybe spread it across two evenings rather than trying to do everyone in one night. That way each relative gets enough time to really share their stories without it feeling rushed or exhausting for them. I don't have strong opinions on the technical audio setup side -- that's more Omar's area -- but I'd just emphasize again that whatever we do file-wise, we need to make sure nothing ends up posted publicly online. As for whether the camcorder can output those WAV specs Omar mentioned, I don't know the specifics of your equipment, so I'll defer to Omar on that question.
